items.title: Next.js: SVG rejection bypass in the image optimization
items.summary: On self-hosted deployments, the Next.js image optimizer ( / next/image ) can be made to process an attacker-supplied SVG even when SVG support is disabled with dangerouslyAllowSVG: false (the default). This reaches an SVG parser the application intended to keep disabled, increasing exposure to denial of service and SVG decoder vulnerabilities.

items.title: Next.js: Cross-client response injection and disclosure in self-hosted Next.js applications forwarding fetched responses
items.summary: Self-hosted Next.js applications (App Router route handlers and the fetch cache) that return a fetched upstream response unchanged can emit a response whose declared framing does not match the body actually sent. items.title: Next.js: Cross-user cache disclosure and poisoning in Next.js use cache with binary arguments
items.summary: Next.js App Router applications that pass binary arguments (such as Uint8Array or Blob values) to functions using the use cache directive can produce identical cache keys for distinct arguments, allowing cached results to be shared across users — cross-user disclosure of cached data or cache poisoning. This affects applications using use cache with binary arguments.

items.title: HtmlSanitizer: CSS Removal DoS
items.summary: Impact An unauthenticated request can occupy one synchronous application worker for seconds. Workarounds Disallow the style attribute.
